conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Standard Rules for Assigning Oxidation Numbers

summaryBox.title: Standard Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: Free elements = 0; Group 1 = +1; Group 2 = +2; F = -1; H = +1 (hydrides = -1); O = -2 (peroxides = -1, superoxides = -1/2, OF₂ = +2).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
OXIDATION NUMBER CORE RULES

1. Free Element: ON = 0 (O₂, P₄, S₈, Fe, Na = 0)
2. Monoatomic Ion: ON = Charge (Na⁺ = +1, Mg²⁺ = +2, Al³⁺ = +3, Cl⁻ = -1)
3. Alkali Metals: +1 | Alkaline Earth Metals: +2
4. Fluorine: Always -1
5. Hydrogen: +1 with non-metals, -1 with active metals (NaH, CaH₂, LiAlH₄)
6. Oxygen: Standard = -2; Peroxide = -1; Superoxide = -1/2; OF₂ = +2; O₂F₂ = +1
conceptBreakdown.content:
The Oxidation Number (ON) is the formal charge an atom retains if all covalent bonds are broken heterolytically assigning shared pairs to the more electronegative atom.

• **Elemental State**: $\text{O}_2, \text{P}_4, \text{S}_8, \text{Fe}(s) = 0$.
• **Fluorine**: Always $-1$.
• **Oxygen Variants**:
  - Normal oxides: $\text{O} = -2$.
  - Peroxides ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$): $\text{O} = -1$ (e.g., $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2, \text{Na}_2\text{O}_2, \text{BaO}_2$).
  - Superoxides: $\text{O} = -1/2$ (e.g., $\text{KO}_2, \text{RbO}_2$).
  - Ozonides: $\text{O} = -1/3$ (e.g., $\text{KO}_3$).
  - Fluorides: $\text{OF}_2 \implies \text{O} = +2$; $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2 \implies \text{O} = +1$.

conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Structural Anomalies & True Oxidation States
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CHROMIUM PEROXIDE (CrO₅) BUTTERFLY STRUCTURE
                      
                                 O (Oxide: -2)
                                 ║
                                 Cr (+6)
                               /  \  \
                              O    O  O    O  <-- 4 Peroxy Oxygens (-1 each)
                              \  /    \  /
                               O        O
                               
   Mathematical Formula: x + 5(-2) = 0 ⟹ x = +10 (IMPOSSIBLE! Max Cr = +6).
   True Structural State: Cr = +6; 4 Peroxy Oxygens (-1), 1 Oxide Oxygen (-2).
conceptBreakdown.content:
When mathematical summation yields impossible values exceeding the valence group limit, structural analysis is mandatory:

1. **Chromium Peroxide ($\text{CrO}_5$)**: Formula gives $\text{Cr} = +10$. Butterfly structure reveals 2 peroxy linkages (4 peroxy oxygens at $-1$, 1 oxide oxygen at $-2$). Thus $\mathbf{\text{Cr} = +6}$.
2. **Caro's Acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$)**: Formula gives $\text{S} = +8$. Structure contains 1 peroxy bond: $2(+1) + x + 3(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \implies \mathbf{\text{S} = +6}$.
3. **Marshall's Acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$)**: Contains 1 peroxy bridge ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$). Both sulfur atoms have $\mathbf{\text{S} = +6}$.
4. **Bleaching Powder ($\text{CaOCl}_2$)**: Mixed salt of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, Hypochlorite ($\text{OCl}^-, \mathbf{\text{Cl} = +1}$), and Chloride ($\text{Cl}^-, \mathbf{\text{Cl} = -1}$). Average $\text{Cl} = 0$.
5. **Tetrathionate ($\text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$)**: Chain $\text{O}_3\text{S}^{(+5)}-\text{S}^{(0)}-\text{S}^{(0)}-\text{SO}_3^{(+5) 2-}$. Two $\text{S} = +5$ and two $\text{S} = 0$. Average $\text{S} = +2.5$.
6. **Magnetite ($\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$)**: Mixed oxide $\text{FeO} \cdot \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$ containing one $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and two $\text{Fe}^{3+}$. Average $\text{Fe} = +8/3$.

quickRevision: Cr in CrO₅ is +6 (butterfly structure with 2 peroxy bonds).
S in Caro's acid (H₂SO₅) and Marshall's acid (H₂S₂O₈) is +6.
CaOCl₂ contains Cl(+1) in OCl⁻ and Cl(-1) in Cl⁻.
S₄O₆²⁻ contains two terminal S(+5) and two central S(0) atoms.
Fe₃O₄ contains one Fe²⁺ and two Fe³⁺ ions.
keyFormulae: \sum \text{ON of all atoms in a neutral molecule} = 0
\sum \text{ON of all atoms in a polyatomic ion} = \text{Charge}
